senses.gloss: J. the prophet. Pesik. Dibré, p. 114ᵇ <he>י׳ ר̇ם̇ י̇ה̇</he> he is named J., because in his days the Lord (Shekhinah) moved from place to place; <cite ref="Yalkut Shimoni on Nach 257:1">Yalk. Jer. 257</cite> <he>י׳ י̇ר̇ם̇ י̇ה̇</he>.
units: <cite ref="Yalkut Shimoni on Nach 257:1">Ib.</cite> … <he>י׳ שבימיו א̇ר̇י̇מ̇י̇ן̇</he> he is called J., because in his days the Temple became deserted; Koh. R. beg., v. <cite ref="A01610"><he>אֱירֶימִיאָה</he></cite>.
<cite ref="Sanhedrin 95a:1">Snh. 95ᵃ</cite>; a. v. fr.—(<he>ספר</he>) <cite ref="T00001"><he>ר׳</he></cite> the Book of Jeremiah.

senses.gloss: name of several Amoraim, esp. R. J., pupil of R. Zera. Ib. 23ᵇ <he>ועל דא אפקוה לר׳ י׳ וכ׳</he> for this (burlesque question) they ejected R. J. from college. Ib. 165ᵇ <he>עיילוה לר׳ י׳ וכ׳</he> upon this (reply) they reinstated R. J.—
units: <cite ref="Jerusalem Talmud Moed Katan 3:1:7">Y. M. Kat. III, 81ᵈ</cite> bot.; a. fr.—V. Fr. M’bo p. 108ᵃ; 118ᵇ
